title: UPPER & LOWER CONTROL ARM
summary: Front suspension upper and lower control arms (A-arms), LH and RH, all models. The upper arm [1] cross shaft is bolted to the frame bracket by bolts [3] and nuts [4] (45-55 lb-ft) with alignment shims [2] between shaft and bracket to set caster and camber; the lower arm [10] cross shaft is bolted to the frame by bolts [5] through special washers [6] into nuts [7] (75-110 lb-ft). Bolts [9] with lock washers [11] at the lower arm pivot are tightened (60-80 lb-ft) with the suspension compressed to alignment height.

fastening.note: Bolt [3] goes through the frame bracket and the upper arm [1] cross shaft; shims [2] sit between shaft and bracket; nut [4] on the bolt from the inboard side. One bolt per shaft end.
Bolt [5] goes down through special washer [6], the lower arm [10] cross shaft and the frame; nut [7] on the bottom.

Bolt [9] with lock washer [11] goes up from below at the lower arm [10] pivot; anchor nut [8] is a two-hole plate nut at the frame next to the pivot. Torque with suspension compressed to the height at which geometry is set (NOTE, triangle 3).

notes: NOTE: Shim to fill gap at each end as required by caster and camber adjustment. Max one each of the two thinner shims (.03 in and .06 in) on any end. Nominal shim pack is 3 × .120 shims.
NOTE (torque 3): Tighten with suspension compressed to height at which geometry is set.
